skill.name: prisma-next-migrations
skill.description: Plan, author, apply, inspect, and recover Prisma Next migrations for Postgres and Mongo, including data transforms, drift, and hash mismatch errors.
skill.summary: Guide Prisma Next migration workflows from planning through safe application and recovery.
skill.author: prisma

security_audit.summary: The Ruby backtick, path traversal, and reconnaissance alerts are scanner false positives caused by Markdown formatting, fixed imports, and documentation links. Database URL usage is confirmed because commands receive sensitive connection credentials. The skill also enables unprompted database mutation and execution of editable migration source, with no prompt injection or exfiltration intent found.

remediation.issue: Migration application can run destructive operations without prompting.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation after showing the target database and destructive plan before running migrate, db update, or db sign.

remediation.issue: Editable migration source is executed with the user's local privileges.
remediation.suggestion: Inspect migration source and repository changes before execution, and use an isolated environment for untrusted repositories.

remediation.issue: Database connection credentials are expanded into command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Use least-privilege database credentials, avoid logging commands, and confirm the selected environment before each database operation.

high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented command applies database changes, and line 214 explicitly states that destructive operations run without a confirmation prompt.

high_findings.title: Execution of Editable Migration Source
high_findings.description: The skill instructs users to execute a repository migration file with Node. A malicious or compromised migration file can run arbitrary code with the agent's privileges.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited workflow directly executes an editable TypeScript migration file. Repository trust and source inspection are not enforced before execution.

content.value_statement: Database changes can fail, drift, or lose data when migration steps are unclear. This skill guides Prisma Next planning, transforms, application, verification, and recovery.
actual_capabilities: Chooses between local db update workflows and formal migration plan workflows.
Explains how to inspect migration plans before applying database changes.
Guides placeholder replacement and data transform authoring in generated migration files.
Covers target-specific migration behavior for Postgres and MongoDB.
Diagnoses hash mismatches, missing markers, schema drift, and partially applied migrations.
Explains migration graph, reference, snapshot, verification, and signing commands.
limitations: The guidance applies to Prisma Next and may not match stable Prisma ORM commands.
The skill cannot determine correct business rules for custom data transformations.
Migration commands can modify live databases and require operator review.
Complex graph review and contract editing are delegated to related Prisma Next skills.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Local Schema Change
use_cases.description: Choose a fast local update or create a reviewable migration package after changing a contract.

use_cases.title: Review a Production Migration
use_cases.description: Inspect planned operations, data transforms, and destructive changes before deployment.

use_cases.title: Recover a Failed Deployment
use_cases.description: Diagnose drift, marker mismatches, hash mismatches, or partial migration state.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Migration Path
prompt_templates.prompt: I changed my Prisma Next contract for [change]. Should I use db update or migration plan? Explain the safest sequence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner choosing between local and formal workflows

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Data Backfill
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a [Postgres or MongoDB] migration for [schema change]. Include the required backfill checks, transform steps, and verification.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a Migration Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose [error code or message] in my Prisma Next migration. Explain likely causes, evidence to inspect, and recovery steps that preserve data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Engineer recovering from a migration failure

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production rollout plan for [migration]. Address graph state, destructive operations, transaction behavior, backups, verification, rollback, and target database differences.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced operator planning a high-impact deployment

output_examples.input: I added an optional field on my local Postgres database. Which workflow should I use?
output: Use the local database update path because the database has no shared migration history.
Preview the operations before applying them.
Switch to a formal migration before sharing or deploying the change.

output_examples.input: My generated migration contains a placeholder for a required column backfill.
output: Open the generated migration source and replace every placeholder with a query-plan closure.
Use a rowset check that identifies remaining invalid rows.
Self-emit the migration package, inspect it, and apply it only after review.

output_examples.input: Migration application reports a hash mismatch.
output_examples.output: The migration artifacts may be stale after source edits. Inspect the package, self-emit it, verify the changed files, then retry the migration.

best_practices: Preview and inspect every migration before applying it to a shared database.
Use one end-contract reference for every data transform query plan.
Back up important data and confirm the database target before destructive operations.
anti_patterns: Do not use direct database updates against shared or production environments.
Do not edit canonical migration artifacts instead of the generated migration source.
Do not run editable migration files from an untrusted repository.

faq.question: When should I use db update?
faq.answer: Use it for a private development database when you do not need replayable migration history.

faq.question: When should I use migration plan?
faq.answer: Use it for shared branches, reviewed changes, production deployments, or changes requiring data transforms.

faq.question: Why does a migration contain placeholders?
faq.answer: The planner detected required data work but cannot infer your business transformation logic.

faq.question: How do I fix a migration hash mismatch?
faq.answer: Inspect the edited migration source, self-emit the package, review regenerated artifacts, and retry.

faq.question: Does the skill support Postgres and MongoDB?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains their different imports, migration factories, markers, and transaction behavior.

faq.question: Can I apply migrations without review?
faq.answer: No. Migration commands may run destructive operations, and formal migration application does not prompt for confirmation.
